# Phase 1 results (auto-generated by src/compare.py)

Copied from the Colab run output on 2026-10-19. That run used a Tesla T4. Every encoder logged
`[cuda ok]`. Extraction took MOMENT 867 s, DINOv2 1578 s and Qwen 501 s. The full logs and JSON
files were written next to the cached embeddings (`results/emb/`, not committed).

## Test-set text statistics (computed locally from the same split)
- 4,000 test reports, of which only 2,225 are unique. 50.9% of test reports have an exact
  duplicate. The most common is "sinus rhythm. normal ecg." with 329 copies.
- Some reports are English, not German. Some carry trailing machine text ("… 4.46 unbestätigter
  bericht").
- If ties among identical reports were broken at random, the best possible exact-match text R@1
  would be about 55.6%. So instance-level TS↔TXT retrieval is partly ill-posed on PTB-XL.
  Label-level (zero-shot diagnostic) retrieval is the better text test.

(R@5/R@10 for lead II are in `results_A_leadII.json` on Drive.)

**Reading:** lead II moves *further* from the paper, with even stronger text alignment. So the lead
choice doesn't explain why our numbers exceed the paper's. Lead II, the main rhythm lead, carries
more diagnostic information than lead I, which fits text alignment improving. TS–IMG barely
changes.

## Label-level evaluation (src/label_eval.py; 5 PTB-XL diagnostic superclasses; 3 seeds; Colab T4)
Test records with at least one diagnostic superclass are used. "Label P@10" is the share of the
top-10 retrieved test reports whose record has the *same superclass set* as the query; chance is
0.223. "Zero-shot AUROC" uses class prototypes = mean projected embedding of single-superclass
train reports; it is the macro AUROC over the 5 classes.

| | Lead I | Lead II |
|---|---|---|
| TS→TXT label P@10 (chance 0.223) | 0.333 ± 0.002 | 0.372 ± 0.004 |
| IMG→TXT label P@10 | 0.318 ± 0.002 | 0.350 ± 0.006 |
| TS zero-shot AUROC (text prototypes) | 0.684 ± 0.003 | 0.726 ± 0.003 |
| IMG zero-shot AUROC | 0.668 ± 0.003 | 0.711 ± 0.006 |
| Untrained heads, TS zero-shot AUROC | 0.516 ± 0.064 | 0.522 ± 0.030 |
| Reference: supervised linear probe on frozen MOMENT features (AUROC) | 0.829 | 0.854 |

**Reading:** the aligned space carries real diagnostic meaning. Zero-shot AUROC is about 0.68–0.73
against 0.5 for untrained heads, and label P@10 is well above chance. It still sits well below
what the frozen MOMENT features support with supervision (0.83–0.85). Contrastive alignment to
reports recovers only part of the diagnostic information the encoder already has. That's a
concrete, measurable gap for the adaptation pilot to target. (Untrained-head label P@10 falls
below chance, 0.10 vs. 0.22, because random projections systematically favor non-matching
reports, so the chance column is the right floor for that metric.)

## Phase-2 pilot, seed 0, lead I (src/adapt.py; matched extra budget ≈295k params; Colab T4)
All arms train on the mean of 2 random windows per step and evaluate on all 10, so the head arm
differs slightly from phase 1 (TS–TXT margin 0.371 vs. 0.386). All three ran 50 epochs.
**This is one seed.**

| Arm | Extra params | Best val loss | TS–TXT margin ↑ | TS–TXT Procrustes ↓ | TS–TXT CKA ↑ | TS–TXT R@1 | TS–IMG R@1 | TS zero-shot AUROC | TS→TXT label P@10 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| head | 0 | 11.19 | 0.371 | 1.183 | 0.297 | 1.26% | 62.2% | 0.687 | 0.330 |
| deep_head (width 191) | 294,335 | 11.22 | 0.368 | 1.191 | 0.294 | 1.23% | 61.2% | 0.685 | 0.331 |
| **lora (r = 8, q/v, 12 layers)** | 294,912 | **11.02** | **0.388** | **1.159** | **0.311** | **1.51%** | **65.9%** | 0.684 | 0.339 |

IMG–TXT (no TS involved) is unchanged across arms (margin 0.370–0.374), as expected.

**Reading (single seed, so provisional):**
1. **Same budget, different place:** spending ~295k parameters on a deeper head does nothing, and
   is even slightly worse. Spending them as LoRA inside MOMENT improves every *geometric* TS
   metric: TS–TXT margin +0.017, Procrustes −0.024, CKA +0.014, TS–TXT R@1 +0.25 points, TS–IMG
   R@1 +3.7 points. That fits the hypothesis that the bottleneck is the encoder's geometry, not the
   readout.
2. **But diagnostic content doesn't move:** zero-shot AUROC stays at 0.684 vs. 0.687, and label
   P@10 rises only +0.009. The gap to the supervised probe (0.83) stays open. LoRA makes TS
   embeddings line up better with their *own* report and plot, but it doesn't make them more
   diagnostic. Better geometric alignment ≠ better downstream semantics. That's the question the
   paper itself raises, and the duplicate-heavy, indirect reports are a likely reason.
3. **Caveats:** one seed. In phase 1 the head-arm seed spread was ≤0.001 on margin, so +0.017 is
   probably real, but LoRA's own seed variance is unknown. A full LoRA run takes about 2.9 h on a
   T4. Lead I only, rank 8 only.

## Steps A + B: objective variants scored with fairer metrics (lead I, 3 seeds each, Colab T4)
`src/train_heads_v2.py` + `src/metrics_v2.py`, on the cached phase-1 embeddings (frozen encoders, heads
only). All variants use the same protocol and stop early on the *standard* InfoNCE val loss.
Means over seeds 0–2 (seed spread ≤ 0.002 on margin and AUROC). TS–TXT pair shown.

| Objective (text pairs) | Cos margin ↑ | Procrustes, paper ↓ | Procrustes, symmetric ↓ | R@1, paper rule | R@1, dup-aware | Zero-shot AUROC ↑ | Label P@10 ↑ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| infonce (paper) | 0.386 | 1.160 | 0.816 | 1.14% | 2.48% | 0.684 | 0.333 |
| dupmask (identical reports = positives) | 0.385 | 1.160 | 0.816 | 1.18% | 2.53% | 0.684 | 0.334 |
| soft (text-similarity soft targets) | 0.320 | 1.271 | 0.856 | 1.16% | 2.30% | **0.722** | 0.327 |
| label (diagnosis = positives; ORACLE, uses labels) | 0.210 | 1.492 | 0.910 | 0.55% | 1.32% | 0.724 | 0.313 |

"R@1, paper rule" = exact-index match with ties broken at random, as the paper's code effectively
does. The phase-1 numbers above counted exact ties as hits, which slightly favours TS→TXT; use this
column for comparisons with the paper.

**Reading:**
1. **The alignment metrics and diagnostic content move in opposite directions.** Moving down the
   table, every paper-style alignment metric gets *worse* (margin 0.386 → 0.210, Procrustes up,
   retrieval down), while zero-shot diagnosis gets *better* (0.684 → 0.72). Ranked by the paper's
   metrics, the most diagnostically useful models come last.
2. **Soft targets from the frozen text encoder reach the label oracle's diagnostic level
   (0.722 vs. 0.724) without using any labels**, while the paper's metrics call them worse than the
   baseline.
3. **Masking exact duplicates does nothing** (dupmask ≈ infonce on every metric). Identical reports
   already map to *identical* text embeddings, so the "false negative" is a symmetric tie the
   standard loss can't act on anyway. What helps is treating *similar but different* reports as
   related.
4. **Symmetric vs. paper Procrustes:** the symmetric version stays in [0, 1] (0.82–0.91 against
   1.16–1.49) and ranks these four objectives the same way. So in this comparison the scale issue
   distorts absolute values but doesn't flip the ordering. Critique #2 stays about interpretability,
   not about this ranking.
5. **Duplicate-aware retrieval roughly doubles R@1** (≈1.1% → ≈2.5%), quantifying how much of the
   paper-rule TS→TXT retrieval failure is ties among identical reports.
